attributes.gen_ai.tool.call.arguments: "{\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Formal verification of target.is_even against spec.md using Z3.\\n\\nApproach: bounded symbolic execution of the Python source by hand.\\n`is_even` is a single straight-line expression, so its semantics is modeled\\ndirectly in Z3 as `r == n % 2 == 0`, and we check that this model is\\nequivalent to the specification \\\"n % 2 == 0\\\" for all bounded integers.\\n\\nTheorem 1 (soundness):  model(n)  ==>  spec(n)\\nTheorem 2 (completeness): spec(n) ==>  model(n)\\n\\nBoth are checked by asking Z3 to refute the negation (i.e., find a\\ncounterexample). `unknown` results are treated as failures.\\n\\nRun:  PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pylibs python verify_is_even.py\\n(adjust PYTHONPATH to wherever z3-solver is installed)\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nimport sys\\n\\nimport z3\\n\\nfrom target import is_even\\n\\n# --- Source model -----------------------------------------------------------\\n# The function body is `return n % 2 == 0`. CPython's % on ints follows\\n# Python semantics: result has the sign of the divisor. For divisor 2,\\n# n % 2 is always 0 or 1, so the result is 1 (truthy) iff n is even.\\n# Z3's (mod n 2) on Ints coincides with Python's n % 2 for divisor 2.\\n\\nn = z3.Int(\\\"n\\\")\\nmodel = (n % 2) == 0  # symbolic model of is_even(n)\\nspec = (n % 2) == 0   # specification from spec.md\\n\\n\\ndef check(name: str, goal: z3.BoolRef) -> z3.CheckSatResult:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Prove `goal` is valid (negation is unsatisfiable).\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    s = z3.Solver()\\n    s.add(z3.Not(goal))\\n    res = s.check()\\n    status = \\\"PROVED\\\" if res == z3.unsat else f\\\"FAILED ({res})\\\"\\n    print(f\\\"{name}: {status}\\\")\\n    if res == z3.sat:\\n        print(\\\"  counterexample:\\\", s.model())\\n    return res\\n\\n\\n# --- Soundness: is_even(n) returns True only when spec holds -----------------\\n# If the function returns True, its body evaluated n % 2 == 0 to True,\\n# which is exactly the spec predicate.\\nr1 = check(\\\"Theorem 1 (soundness): model(n) ==> spec(n)\\\", z3.Implies(model, spec))\\n\\n# --- Completeness: whenever spec holds, the function returns True ------------\\n# Same symbolic content, so this holds trivially for the model.\\nr2 = check(\\\"Theorem 2 (completeness): spec(n) ==> model(n)\\\", z3.Implies(spec, model))\\n\\n# --- Consistency with the actual Python implementation -----------------------\\n# Exhaustive concrete check on a bounded range, cross-checking that our Z3\\n# model matches the real function's behavior (guards against modeling error).\\nfor k in range(-1000, 1001):\\n    assert is_even(k) == ((k % 2) == 0), f\\\"model mismatch at n={k}\\\"\\nprint(\\\"Concrete cross-check on n in [-1000, 1000]: OK\\\")\\n\\nif r1 != z3.unsat or r2 != z3.unsat:\\n    sys.exit(1)\\nprint(\\\"ALL THEOREMS PROVED\\\")\\n\",\"path\":\"verify_is_even.py\"}"

attributes.gen_ai.tool.call.arguments: "{\"content\":\"# Verification Plan for `target.is_even`\\n\\n**Spec under verification** (`spec.md`): *For all integers n, is_even(n) returns True if and only if n % 2 == 0.*\\n\\n**Verification target** (`target.py`):\\n\\n```python\\ndef is_even(n: int) -> bool:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Return True if and only if n is even.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    return n % 2 == 0\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Chosen approach: Z3 SMT proof with hand-translated semantics\\n\\n**Tool:** Z3 via the `z3-solver` Python bindings, driven by a script\\n(`verify_is_even.py`) that encodes the function's semantics as an SMT\\nformula and proves equivalence with the spec by refutation.\\n\\n**Why this approach:**\\n- The function is a single straight-line expression with no loops, recursion,\\n  mutation, or exception paths. A full deductive verifier (Dafny, Why3, Frama-C)\\n  would add heavyweight trusted components (VC generators, assertion languages)\\n  with little gain for one predicate.\\n- Z3 directly decides the resulting formulas over unbounded integers, so we get\\n  a genuine universal proof (\\\"for all n\\\") \u2014 stronger than exhaustive testing.\\n- The Python API makes the encoding auditable line-by-line.\\n\\n## 2.
